name: caption_ink
description: Make captions readable over light cards (the graphics covering a caption's band: an opaque overlay, a 3D scene with a backdrop, or an overlay whose pixels cover the band, such as frame_broll's paper matte). Reads the backdrop from the card's own render (a JSX card) or from one frame without captions per 3D item, measures it in the rows the caption draws in, and writes ink ("dark" over a light card, "light" over a dark one) and inkAuto ({card, ink, backdrop}: what it wrote and the luminance it measured) on the caption, so the editor, sample_frame and the export draw the same. Footage is left to the style. An ink is this step's only while inkAuto names the same ink; any other ink is a person's and never changed. Ink this step wrote is cleared when the card is gone. A caption whose words lie over different cards (or over a card and footage) is split at the word nearest the edge, one caption per run of words, each inked on its own; a person's captions, translated ones and those with translations are never split. A caption inked dark that shows over footage for a frame or more before its card starts or after it ends is snapped to the card's edge (its start or end, and its words clamped inside); one whose snap would leave a word no time on screen is left light. A single word at a caption's edge, over footage, splits off however short. Does nothing for plate and subtitle. generate_captions runs it when the project has a card. Writes the captions only; a caption edit since it read them is refused.

input.description: The project id, its folder, or the absolute path of its project.json

output.description: {dark, light, cleared, kept, split, snapped, changed, warnings?}: captions set dark, set light, cleared, and left as they are (a person's, or one whose snap would leave a word no time on screen); split is the captions split at a card's edge (their pieces count in dark and light); snapped is the captions (or pieces) snapped to their card's edge; changed is whether anything was written.

params.name: project
params.description: The project id, its folder, or the absolute path of its project.json
